body:
## The concrete case that hit this

PR link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template#13 adds a Security workflow whose `dependency-review` job failed in CI with:

> Dependency review is not supported on this repository. Please ensure that Dependency graph is enabled, see https://github.com/link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/settings/security_analysis

The repository's **Dependency graph** toggle on
https://github.com/link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/settings/security_analysis
was off. There is **no REST or GraphQL endpoint** that enables or disables it:
the only place the toggle exists is the web UI — which is exactly gh-manager's
charter ("the operations the REST and GraphQL APIs do not expose").

## What I actually had to do

1. `gh api -X PUT /repos/{owner}/{repo}/vulnerability-alerts` (this one *does*
   have an API) — after which `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom`
   started returning an SBOM, i.e. the dependency graph came on as a side
   effect of enabling vulnerability alerts. That worked by luck of the
   prerequisite chain, not by a supported operation, and it is not documented
   or guaranteed: for other repos (org-enforced code security policies,
   private repos, default-setup-managed repos) the UI checkbox is genuinely
   the only path.
2. Re-ran the failed CI job.

## Request

Add a `security` command family that drives the
`/settings/security_analysis` page, browser-write + API-verify like the
package commands:

```bash
# No API exists at all -> browser write, verified via SBOM endpoint afterwards
gh-manager security dependency-graph <owner>/<repo> --enable
gh-manager security dependency-graph <owner>/<repo> --disable

# These have REST endpoints, but the toggles live on the same page, so cover
# the whole page for one-stop repo setup (API-backed where available):
gh-manager security vulnerability-alerts <owner>/<repo> --enable      # PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/vulnerability-alerts
gh-manager security automated-security-fixes <owner>/<repo> --enable  # PUT /repos/{o}/{r}/automated-security-fixes
gh-manager security secret-scanning <owner>/<repo> --enable
gh-manager security push-protection <owner>/<repo> --enable
```

Reads should be API where the API exists (204/404 on
`GET .../vulnerability-alerts`, SBOM presence for the dependency graph) and
browser for the rest, with the same verification philosophy as
`package public`: write, re-read, prove the write landed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `gh-manager security dependency-graph org/repo --enable` flips the
      toggle and `GET /repos/org/repo/dependency-graph/sbom?ref=<default>`
      returns an SBOM within the verification window
- [ ] A toggle gh-manager could not flip (e.g. org policy override) fails
      loudly with the screenshot + HTML in `~/.gh-manager/logs/`, non-zero
      exit
- [ ] Mutations require confirmation or `--yes`, consistent with the
      existing destructive-operation policy
- [ ] Meaningful exit codes distinguishing "already enabled" from "enabled"
      (idempotent re-run should not be an error)

## Why one issue for the whole page

The dependency graph was this repo's blocker, but the same setup dance is
needed for every new template repo in the org (php/python/js
ai-driven-development-pipeline-template siblings), and each of them wants the
full security_analysis page in a known state. One command family covering the
page turns "open ten settings URLs per repo" into a script.
title: Support managing repository Code security & analysis settings (dependency graph and friends)
